# pnpm registry route golden fixtures

Hosted mode can route a patched npm package through a pnpm named registry:
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` declares the patch server's registry of each patch
(`namedRegistries`, `socket-<first digits of the patch UUID>`) and overrides
each patched release with its own
(`'<name>@<version>': 'socket-<id>:<version>'`). pnpm records such a release under
its own lock key and records the overrides in the lock, so the scan rewrites
`pnpm-lock.yaml` to what pnpm itself writes, without running pnpm. These
fixtures pin that rewrite to real pnpm, byte for byte.

Each case directory holds:

- `project/`: the project as real pnpm locked it before any patch
  (`package.json` files, every `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and the
  `pnpm-workspace.yaml` the project already has, if any);
- `patches.json`: the patches a scan is granted (name, version, patch uuid,
  tarball URL, the registry address, which is the directory the tarball is
  served from, and the patched tarball's sha512);
- `expected/`: every `pnpm-lock.yaml` as real pnpm resolves it once the
  workspace file routes those patches, and that `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (written
  the way the scan writes it; the tests assert the scan writes the same
  bytes);
- `refuses.txt`, in two cases only: pnpm does not lock that project as a
  respelling of the plain lock, so the scan stays off the route and gives
  this reason. `expected/` is then the generating pnpm's lock, kept as the
  record of what pnpm does (in `peer-variants`, pnpm 11 and pnpm 12 differ).

Regenerate with real pnpm executables (>= 11.20), no network needed:

```sh
node scripts/gen-pnpm-registry-override-golden.mjs <pnpm> [<pnpm>...]
```

The first executable writes the fixtures; every other one must produce
byte-identical lockfiles or the script fails. The committed fixtures were
written by pnpm 12.22.0 and are identical on 11.20.0, 11.25.0, 11.28.13,
12.0.0, 12.4.2, 12.10.0, 12.16.0, 12.19.0 and 12.21.0. `pinned-pnpm` records
the pnpm that wrote it (pnpm 12's two-document lock), so it is generated by
pnpm 12 alone.

The tests that read them: `formats::pnpm::registry_alias` (the lock rewrite
and its inverse), `formats::pnpm::named_registries` (the workspace file), and
`hosted::engine::tests::the_registry_route_writes_what_pnpm_writes` (the whole
scan).
